text:
Muscle lactate production increases when the rate of glycolysis exceeds the mitochondria's capacity to oxidize pyruvate. This happens during high-intensity exercise, when oxygen supply is limited (hypoxia), or when ATP demand is high, so pyruvate is converted to lactate by lactate dehydrogenase to regenerate NAD⁺. In short, it rises with intense or anaerobic exercise.

CONFIDENCE: 60
